previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease status post bypass, diabetes, and transfusion-dependent anemia was admitted due to severe fatigue and low hematocrit (20.8%) detected during a routine dialysis session. The patient had recently returned from a six-week trip where he missed epoetin alfa therapy. He experienced brief chest pain in the emergency department, consistent with demand ischemia from anemia, which resolved with transfusion. He received packed red blood cell transfusion on hospital day one and underwent scheduled hemodialysis on day two. His hematocrit improved to 26%, symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home on day three in stable condition. Medication adjustments included increasing lisinopril and switching from ranitidine to pantoprazole for better gastrointestinal protection. The patient was advised to resume epoetin alfa, continue all home medications, and follow up with his nephrologist and cardiologist.
